explanation: Replacing memset with a trivial NULL guard removes zero-initialization of the CPUInfo struct. Callers that rely on fields being zero-initialized (e.g. checking info->x86.sse) will read uninitialized stack memory, causing undefined behavior / MSan findings.

Omitting the zeroing of *edx in the fallback path of cpuinfo_x86 leaves edx uninitialized when CPUID is unavailable or the requested level is unsupported. Downstream code reads flags_edx to set SSE/SSE2/CMov/MMX fields, reading garbage stack data.

Changing <= to < in the lag bounds assertion means lag==MAX_LAG passes the assert but the subsequent vst1q_f64 stores (e.g. autoc+12 writing 2 doubles) write past an autoc buffer sized for MAX_LAG elements, causing OOB write.
Changing >>58 to >>57 doubles the index range from 0-63 to 0-127 for the 64-entry DEBRUIJN_IDX64 array, causing out-of-bounds reads when the upper bits of the de Bruijn hash select indices 64-127.

Off-by-one in SIMD loop bound: changing data_len-7 to data_len-6 allows one extra 8-element iteration when data_len is a multiple of 8, causing _mm256_storeu_si256 to write 32 bytes past the end of the residual buffer.

Off-by-one in wide SIMD loop bound for order==12: changing data_len-3 to data_len-2 allows one extra 4-element iteration when data_len is a multiple of 4, causing _mm_storeu_si128 to write 16 bytes past the end of the residual buffer.

Off-by-one in the order==4 NEON loop bound: changing -11 to -10 allows one extra iteration where vld1q_s32(data + i + 7) reads 4 int32s past data_len - 11, causing an out-of-bounds read of up to 4 bytes beyond the allocated buffer.
Removing the sum=0 initialization before the switch-case scalar fallback causes use of uninitialized memory when computing residual, potentially leaking stack data into output.

Off-by-one in SIMD loop bound: changing data_len-3 to data_len-1 allows _mm_storeu_si128 to write 4 int32s (16 bytes) into residual when only 1-2 elements remain, causing a heap-buffer-overflow of up to 2 elements past the end of residual[].
Off-by-one in seektable read loop: i <= num_points instead of i < num_points writes one extra SeekPoint entry past the heap-allocated array

Removed 4-element guard padding from output buffer allocation: safe_malloc_muladd2_ allocates size+0 instead of size+4 elements, but output pointer is still offset by +4, causing all subsequent sample writes to land 16 bytes before the allocation
